steps.description: The hypothesis posits that non-linear transcendental constraint systems exhibit "intermediate rigidity" where $N_c(w)$ trends flat for small $w$ but increases for large $w$. This is a direct contrast to the rigid linear case (flat) and the fat polynomial case (increasing). I will implement the capacity_scan framework to rigorously test this. First, I will verify zero-errability with a simple linear anchor (rigid case). Then I will construct the non-linear transcendental family (e.g., $\sin(wx) = y$) and scan widths to measure the $N_c(w)$ trend. I expect to observe an increasing trend for large $w$ as the network struggles to resolve the accumulating topological features of the transcendental solution space, confirming the intermediate rigidity hypothesis.
